evidence.claim: myInstances, myExpertSites, myExpertSite, myExpertSiteDeployment, myAgentWorkspace, myDomains, myWallet, myInvoices, myCatalogOrders, opsEvents and myPodOpenclawStatus all exist as per-user GraphQL queries.

Lifecycle mutations exist: provisionExpertSite, deployExpertSite, stopExpertSiteDeployment, publishExpertSite, manageAgentWorkspace, manageCatalogOrder, addDomain, renewDomain, setDomainAutoRenew, topUpInstance, payInvoice.
rebuild, reprovision, wipe and fleet-upgrade are HTTP endpoints behind PlatformOperatorHttpGuard - operator only, and write-only. There is no operator READ surface at all.
PlatformRole.Operator is checked in exactly one place and by no GraphQL resolver.
MyInstance.ram and vcpu are hardcoded null even though instances.ram_mb and instances.vcpu exist.
getBurnUsd is the ONLY aggregate in the codebase: SUM(amount_usd) GROUP BY instance WHERE kind='consumption', reconciled from OpenRouter every 10 minutes.
The /provisioning page shipped at revision 1.4 with a sealed four-state matrix and a same-state parity pass against production.

unknowns: Whether the console's home route stays /provisioning or becomes /resources. The shipped route is /provisioning and renaming it is a customer-visible address change; Preview must decide and record it.

Whether an operator viewing a customer's resource is a real scenario. The danger zone is drawn for an operator, but no operator READ surface exists, so today an operator reaching a detail page would be reading their OWN resources.
Whether creditBurnUsd belongs on the resource detail page, on billing, or both. It is lifetime-to-date rather than per-cycle and is always null for agent workspaces.
Whether the sidebar's per-section counts are worth their cost: no count query exists, so each is either derived from a list the console already fetched or a second request.

directions.thesis: A fixed sidebar of resource KINDS, a list as the console's home, and a full page per resource. Light actions ride the row; heavy and destructive ones live on the detail page where there is room to say what they do.
directions.primaryCta: Cấp phát mới on the list; the per-resource lifecycle action on the detail page
readingOrder: list heading with count and primary action
one resource: identity, facts, actions, danger zone
tradeoffs: The most routes of the three, and a sidebar with four sections looks empty on an account holding two resources.
Needs the three sidebar contracts that blocked the previous Apply run.
A row shows infrastructure facts, so it depends on vCPU/RAM which myInstances currently hardcodes to null.
legacyDivergence: None within the baseline. The shipped /provisioning page is absorbed as the console's resource list with its sealed anatomy intact - same frame key, same FleetRow, same filter, same counter strip, same four states. What is added sits around it (a sidebar) and below it (a detail route); the approved render itself is unchanged.
